inventory_gate: Do not execute until source inventory reconciliation and resource permit are approved by the owning runner.
shared_setup: Record exact source SHA, built extension artifact hash/version, Chrome version, extension ID, admin identity, timestamp, and owned disposable profile. Load that exact artifact and confirm the sidepanel uses it; repeat after extension and target-page reload.

Serve an owned localhost HTTP page with a visible unique fixture marker, output area, and counter initialized to 0. Its own page script must inspect the actual navigator.modelContext object and registerTool/getTools/tools/callTool members on every load, record their observed shape, and register a uniquely named benign tool only when native registerTool is present. Give that tool an inputSchema for {nonce:string} and a run implementation that increments the visible counter once and returns {nonce,counter,fixtureMarker}; read the page DOM separately after calls. Use no navigator.modelContext polyfill or fake API. If the observed native API shape cannot support the proposed registration/list/call fixture, mark the native positive unverified and open a defect lead for source/API mismatch rather than claiming a pass.

Keep malformed JSON and valid but schema-invalid JSON distinct: the Tools form parser rejects malformed text before handler execution; a real dispatcher schema gate must receive syntactically valid non-object JSON to demonstrate schema rejection. A direct manual handler.run call cannot prove dispatcher validation or permission enforcement.

For each manual Tools run, first focus the owned page tab and verify its marker. Keep another tab with a different marker open. The manual runner has assignedTabId:null and resolves the currently focused tab; a dispatcher/agent run latches assignedTabId and must stay on its original tab if focus changes, or return No active tab if it closes.

Record original page tool catalog/counter and cleanup by closing the disposable page/profile or unregistering the owned tool if the actual API supports it. Never invoke tools registered by unrelated pages.

steps: On the native fixture page, Tools > webmcp_check_availability > Run with {}. Compare available with direct observation of navigator.modelContext. Compare tool_count only with modelContext.tools array length when that array exists; this handler does not call getTools(), whereas the list handler prefers getTools().

Try malformed JSON in the Tools form and record form-parser rejection before handler execution. Separately pass syntactically valid non-object JSON through the real dispatcher schema gate; capture its schema rejection without counting direct handler.run as validation.

Run on an owned page without navigator.modelContext in the same real browser, if available, expecting available:false and tool_count:0; no fake deletion or replacement of the API. Also test a restricted chrome:// tab and no selected tab, expecting a bounded ok:false reason rather than a crash.
Reload page and extension, reconfirm build receipt, focus fixture, rerun and compare response; verify the separate tab marker was never consulted.
expected: Native positive requires direct browser feature observation and available:true. If tools is an array, tool_count matches its length; if only getTools() exists, record tool_count:0 as this handler's source limitation, not catalog parity or native unavailability. If API absent or shape incompatible, leave native-positive unresolved and record a defect lead.
Manual runner alone proves only direct handler execution; admin/member/guest permission outcomes require dispatcher and UI access checks in a separate authorized execution phase.

steps: After native registration succeeds, focus fixture tab and run webmcp_list_page_tools with {} in Tools. Compare count and the uniquely named tool's name, description and input_schema with direct page getTools() when present, otherwise tools array; redact unrelated names from evidence.

Try malformed JSON in the Tools form and require form-parser rejection before execution; separately send syntactically valid non-object JSON through dispatcher validation and record schema rejection. On a browser/page without native modelContext, verify {ok:false,reason:'WebMCP unavailable'}; on a restricted tab verify a bounded scripting error.

Reload the owned page: its own script must re-register the benign tool using the observed native API. If it does not, re-establish the fixture with that same native API before any post-reload assertion; a DevTools-only registration is not assumed to persist. Reload extension, rerun with fresh receipt, confirm fixture tool appears once and unrelated second-tab tool is absent.
expected: Native positive requires an actual page registration plus matching list content; an empty list or unavailable branch is only a negative result.
The manual result does not prove non-admin rejection or agent advertisement; preserve those as separate dispatcher checks.

steps: With the owned native tool present, record counter N. In Tools run {"name":"<unique fixture tool>","arguments":{"nonce":"<unique nonce>"}}. Check {ok:true,result:{nonce,counter:N+1,fixtureMarker}} and independently read visible page counter N+1; verify no change in the second tab.

Call an unknown tool name and malformed page-tool args; require ok:false with bounded reason and unchanged counter. Submit missing or empty name through dispatcher schema validation; malformed JSON must fail in the Tools form.

Check API-absent page returns WebMCP unavailable and restricted tab yields scripting error without side effect. Reload page and extension; require the owned page script to re-register through the observed native API, or re-establish that fixture before the post-reload assertion. Establish new counter baseline and repeat native call once with a new nonce.
expected: Native positive requires both returned content and independent page side-effect readback; unavailable, unknown-tool, or mocked API results are not positives.
Action-tier permission and Ask/Act confirmation behavior require real dispatcher/agent execution, not the manual runner.

steps: In Tools run {"action":"check"} and {"action":"list" on the owned native fixture. Compare delegated responses with leaf cases and independently inspected API/catalog; these branches resolve read tier via tierFor.

Run {"action":"call","tool_name":"<unique fixture tool>","arguments":{"nonce":"<unique nonce>"}}; require matching result and independently observed counter increment. After page and extension reload, confirm the owned page script re-registered via the observed native API, or re-establish that fixture, then repeat with a fresh receipt.

Run call without tool_name and with unknown name; require bounded handler failure and unchanged counter. Submit invalid action and syntactically valid non-object JSON through the dispatcher schema gate; require schema rejection. Submit malformed JSON in the Tools form; require form-parser rejection before execution. Check API-absent and restricted-tab responses.

In separately authorized dispatcher flow, verify guest cannot open Tools, member cannot invoke admin-only tool, admin check/list are read-tier, admin call is action-tier with correct Ask/Act control, and assigned tab stays pinned while focused tab changes. Capture actual authorization and confirmation UI outcomes rather than treating manual runs as proof.
expected: All three canonical branches must use their corresponding leaf handler and page fixture. Positive call needs return-content and side-effect readback.

The canonical tool has no direct required_permissions entry in the inventory, while its leaves require activeTab and scripting; runtime Chrome scripting failures and dispatcher permission behavior must be recorded separately.
